Ontario Auto Insurance Minimums Explained

You said

What Auto Insurance Broker / Company will allow for underwriting the minimum auto insurance in Ontario for $200,000, rather than $1 Million being the lowest allowable as policy?

Here is the industry secret: legally, every single licensed auto insurance company in Ontario is required to sell you a policy with the $200,000 statutory minimum liability limit.

If you have tried to get a quote for $200,000 and been told, "Our company policy is $1 Million minimum," you have run into a massive, highly frustrating industry grey area. Standard insurers and brokers routinely claim they cannot write $200,000 policies, but doing so technically puts them in breach of Ontario's strict consumer protection laws.

Why Insurers and Brokers Give You the Runaround

Insurers don't want to sell you a $200,000 policy, and brokers don't want to write them. Here is why they fight you on it:

  • E&O (Errors and Omissions) Risk: If a broker sells you a $200,000 policy and you get into an accident where the damages exceed that limit, you can turn around and sue the broker for failing to advise you of the financial danger. To protect themselves, many brokerages have internal corporate rules refusing to quote anything below $1 Million.

  • System Blocks: Direct writers (like Belairdirect, Sonnet, or CAA) hardcode their online quoting portals to lock the slider at $1 Million or $500,000 so you can't easily select the bare minimum.

How to Actually Secure a $200,000 Policy

If you want to force a standard insurer to give you the statutory minimum, you have to bypass the websites and speak to them directly.

1. The Standard Market Route (The "Magic Words")

Call a broker or a direct writer on the phone. Tell them you want to write a standard Ontario Automobile Policy (OAP 1) with the statutory minimum of $200,000. If they claim they cannot do it, use this leverage:

"Under FSRA’s Take-All-Comers rule, you are legally required to provide me a quote and write the policy at the statutory minimum if I meet your approved underwriting guidelines. I would like to proceed with the $200,000 limit."

2. Use the "Broker Sign-Off" (Your Secret Weapon)

To get a reluctant broker to cooperate, offer to sign an E&O Liability Waiver (sometimes called a "sign-off"). This is a simple document where you explicitly acknowledge that the broker advised you to take a higher limit, but you chose to decline it against their advice. Once the broker's legal liability is covered, their resistance will disappear.

3. The Non-Standard & High-Risk Market (No Fight Required)

If you do not want to fight a standard insurer, the high-risk market writes $200,000 policies all day long:

  • Specialty Insurers (e.g., Coachman, Echelon, Jevco, Pafco): Accessed through independent brokers, these companies specialize in non-standard risk. Because their base rates are already very high, they routinely offer $200,000 limits to help drivers keep their monthly premiums affordable.

  • Facility Association (The Insurer of Last Resort): If no standard market will take you, any licensed broker can place you with the Facility Association. As a government-regulated pool, they are legally mandated to write policies at the absolute bare-bones statutory minimums.

⚠️ A Quick Reality Check: While $200,000 is legally compliant, it is incredibly risky. If you hit a high-end electric vehicle, or if someone in the other car suffers an injury requiring physical therapy, a $200,000 limit will be exhausted almost instantly. Once that $200,000 is gone, the courts can go after your personal assets, savings, and future wages to cover the rest.

💡 The 2026 Strategy to Save Even More Money

If you are looking to slash your insurance bill, don't just focus on the liability limit. Under the Ontario Auto Insurance Reforms, only medical, rehabilitation, and attendant care benefits remain mandatory. You can now completely opt out of optional coverages like Income Replacement, Caregiver Benefits, and Housekeeping Benefits. This is often a much safer way to drop your monthly premium than lowering your liability limit to $200,000.
